what_happened.line: The Historical Commission voted unanimously by roll call to accept all the amendments to the demolition delay bylaw.
The amendments add a penalty per day, each day a separate violation, enforced by the building commissioner.
The spring warrant closed March 15, so the amendments wait for a fall town meeting; the chair will notify the planning board.
Cemetery work was discussed: stump grinding at Goodrich waits for the tree bill, and wall base work cannot happen before fall.
Members will meet separately at the historical society to review a town survey binder found there; the next meeting is April 22 at 7 pm.

why_it_matters: The change would give the town a stronger tool against demolishing old buildings without the delay review, but it takes effect only if a fall town meeting approves it.
Cemetery wall repairs are limited by the money left in the appropriation, so that work is pushed to fall.
watch_next: A fall town meeting warrant article on the demolition delay bylaw amendments.
The commission's next meeting, April 22, 2021 at 7 pm.

what_happened.line: The Historical Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the demolition application for 11 The Clearing, letting demolition proceed at the owner's convenience.
Members agreed to seek the demolition delay bylaw amendments at the fall special town meeting if they miss the annual town meeting warrant.
The chair will contact other commissions and boards to build consensus for promoting the Community Preservation Act to the select board; no vote was taken.
Members will informally look at houses from the 1833 map as a start toward an endangered list, and will first draft their own town survey plan.
The commission approved the December 17, 2020 minutes and set its next meeting for Thursday, March 25, at 7 p.m.

why_it_matters: The Community Preservation Act, if adopted, would add a local funding source for historic projects such as reusing the Primary School, and adopting it is a vote residents would be asked to take.
The demolition delay bylaw amendments would change how long a historic building waits before it can be torn down, and they need a town meeting article to take effect.
watch_next: Commission meeting on Thursday, March 25, at 7 p.m., with the survey plan outline due.
Whether the demolition delay amendments make the annual town meeting warrant or move to the fall special town meeting.
